questions.question: How can you reduce head and neck injuries?
questions.explanation: A good helmet greatly reduces the risk of head and neck injuries. It is your best protection against injury in an accident.

questions.question: What should you do before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle?

options.text: Ride it like your own bike, since all bikes are the same.
Check the controls and shift pattern.
Trust the owner that everything works.
Assume you know where all the controls are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the controls and shift pattern.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle, check the controls and learn the gear pattern. Test the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times.

questions.question: What kind of soles should your motorcycle riding shoes have?

options.text: Material that lets your feet breathe.

questions.explanation: Choose riding boots or shoes that are tall and sturdy to cover and support your ankles. The soles should be made of hard, durable, slip-resistant material.

questions.question: How can you increase your chances of being seen at an intersection?

options.text: Swerve within your lane to get attention.

questions.explanation: Using your headlight and riding in a good lane position helps other drivers see you. Keep space around your motorcycle so you can move out of danger if needed.

questions.question: Why should you maintain a safe distance behind other vehicles?

options.text: To give yourself time and space to see and react to dangers.
So traffic counters can count you as a vehicle.
To encourage other drivers to cut you off.

questions.correctAnswerText: To give yourself time and space to see and react to dangers.
questions.explanation: A safe following distance gives you enough space to stop or swerve if the vehicle ahead stops suddenly. It also helps you see hazards on the road, like potholes.

questions.question: What material should you look for in a protective jacket or pants?
questions.explanation: Wear long pants and a jacket to cover your arms and legs while riding. Leather provides the best protection.

questions.question: What type of sign is rectangular?
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs and other road rules are rectangular. They are white with black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes?

options.text: You don't need to check your blind spot if you use your mirrors.
Mirrors give you a full view of the road around your motorcycle.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
Assume drivers will respond correctly to your turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. Always turn your head and look over your shoulder to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: Where should you get information about your motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Your owner's manual is the best source for information about your specific motorcycle. It includes details about how to operate it and how to maintain it.

questions.question: Who is most likely to crash?

options.text: Those who have completed a safety course.

questions.explanation: Crashes happen most often with new, untrained riders who don't know their motorcycle well.

questions.question: The body gets rid of about how much alcohol per hour?
questions.explanation: Your body can eliminate about one drink per hour on average.

questions.question: What is a good way to lower the risk of a crash?

options.text: Signal to other drivers to show what you plan to do.
Do not look ahead while riding.
Ride in positions that are hard to see.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal to other drivers to show what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure other drivers can see you. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show your intentions. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: What should you do when riding on bridge grating?

options.text: Always ride on the far right side of the lane.
Always ride on the far left side of the lane.
Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Bridge grating may cause your motorcycle to weave slightly. This is normal and not dangerous. Stay relaxed and ride at a steady speed. Do not zigzag, as this is dangerous and makes you swerve out of your lane.

questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Look ahead and watch for dangers before you reach them.
Focus on the controls and speedometer instead of the road.
Not worry about hazards because roads are safe.
Look ahead but try not to watch for dangers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and watch for dangers before you reach them.
questions.explanation: Always look far ahead to spot dangers early. This helps you react before you reach a hazard.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.explanation: Wear reflective and bright clothing at all times when riding. Crashes happen day and night, so stay visible whenever you ride.

questions.question: If you wait one hour after one drink, can you safely ride?

options.text: Yes, your riding skills will not be affected.
No, alcohol effects may still be present.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, alcohol effects may still be present.
questions.explanation: Your body removes about one drink per hour on average, but the time varies by person. Do not ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: How noticeable is a motorcycle's brake light?

options.text: More noticeable than a car's brake lights.
Less noticeable than a car's brake lights.
Less important than a car's brake lights.
More easily seen than a car's brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Less noticeable than a car's brake lights.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is not as noticeable as a car's brake light. Flash your brake light before you slow down or stop to help other drivers see you.

questions.question: What is a simple way to make your motorcycle easier to see?

options.text: Attach a large flag to the frame.

questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on at all times. Also wear bright, reflective clothing and use your turn signals and brake light.

questions.question: Which helmet type is the safest?
questions.explanation: A full-face helmet is the safest because it protects your face and chin in a crash. Half-shell and three-quarter-shell helmets do not.

questions.question: Which item does not protect a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Wear a DOT-approved helmet, face protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, ankle-covering boots, and durable gloves for protection.

questions.question: What should an approved helmet allow you to do?

options.text: See far enough to the sides for safe riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: See far enough to the sides for safe riding.
questions.explanation: A helmet approved by the U.S. Department of Transportation will not limit your vision. You can see as much as you need for safe riding.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When does alcohol start to impair your ability to ride?

options.text: At about half the legal limit.

questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect your ability to ride safely. You can be impaired before reaching the legal limit. Do not drink any alcohol before riding.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.explanation: Bright and reflective clothing makes you more visible in all conditions. Most motorcycle crashes happen during daylight, so wear bright clothing during the day too.

questions.question: When approaching a bump or pothole, why should you rise slightly off your seat?

options.text: So you can jump off if needed.
So your legs can absorb the shock.
So other drivers can see you better.
So you can see the surface better.

questions.correctAnswerText: So your legs can absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: Rising off your seat lets your body absorb some of the impact. This prevents the impact from throwing you off the motorcycle.
